title: Filo Development Plan: Broken
text: “So this is where you were.”
Then a Siltvelt envoy who normally handled miscellaneous chores around the tent came over.
“Shield Hero-sama, thank you so very much for bringing back Éclair-sama, daughter of Seaetto, today. I believe Siltvelt intends to express its gratitude for this quite prominently.”
“She’s that important a person, huh, Éclair-san.”
“By the way, if Father earns too much fame in Melromarc, he’ll die in prison, I say.”
At my words, Father’s brow furrowed in trouble.
“I think I’d heard something like that, but honestly, I’m just glad we managed to save her in time. Even if it makes my position worse.”
“Yes. It seems you’re also concerned about the matter of the slave trade—shall I explain it on your behalf?”
“Then… I suppose I’ll take you up on that.”
“Understood. Though… Shion, or should I say Liberacion-sama? To think he turned out to be the orphaned child of the one said to have been Seaetto’s right-hand man.”
“Is he really that famous?”
At Father’s question, the Siltvelt envoy nodded.

“Yes. According to what the late Seaetto once said, he is the original stock and last descendant of a lineage of lizardmen who served the ancient Shield Hero with utmost loyalty… though over the long course of history their numbers dwindled, until he was the very last one left.”
“Waah…”
“Indeed, it’s undeniable that his build is unlike anything seen among lizardmen these days. I caught a brief glimpse of him myself once before—he bears quite a resemblance.”
The Siltvelt envoy nodded repeatedly, clearly recalling having seen Alligator Guy in his alligator-man form before.
“He was called a half-breed, though…”
“Yes, the story goes that he was born of a union with a human wife. So it seems the Shield Hero’s influence came through strongly, and his beastman blood surfaced as a result.”

The Siltvelt envoy called this a good thing, but Father wore a complicated expression. He seemed to hold the view that the environment which shaped Alligator Guy ought to be respected too. Come to think of it, Father placed great weight on letting people choose things for themselves—he’d been the same way with Big Sister and the others. Class Ups and the like were no exception; he was fundamentally the type who insisted people choose for themselves. He was probably worried about how Alligator Guy himself felt about the human blood flowing within him.
“Even so… I wonder if there’s such a thing as fate at work here. To think one of the slaves I was introduced to turned out to have such an ancestry—it’s astonishing.”
“Yeah…”

There had been a loop before where Father had purchased only Alligator Guy. Big Sister, recalling her own meeting with Father, shuddered at the memory. Had things gone even slightly differently, I might have ended up calling Alligator Guy “Brother-in-law.” But—here’s the thing to be careful of—if that guy and Father were the ones raising Filo-tan, she’d end up with a rather American sort of vibe. Somehow I could picture Father’s face taking on that kind of look too, which was frightening. Conversely, maybe Father would end up as the mascot character in that scenario. In the filter of my mind, Father from that loop had shrunk down to peckul size. A plush-toy Father, if you will. Would we eventually end up in that loop too…? If possible, I’d like Filo-tan to remain Filo-tan.
“Since that’s how it turned out for Shion, maybe Raphtalia-chan and Theo actually have some special birth secret too, you never know.”

Father laughed it off with an “ahaha,” but in my mind’s eye, Big Sister’s face said this was no laughing matter. Ah, right—Ark or Hou-kun might know something about that. Tell us, know-it-all Hou-kun. In my memory, Hou-kun was saying, “What are you expecting from me? I’m not doing it!”—but I firmly believe that if you just asked nicely, Hou-kun would come through.
“Vau?”
“Wolf too, apparently.”
“Vau!”
Would such mysteries ever come to light, I wondered? Well, if they did, I’d make sure to have the information ready to pass along to Father come the next loop.
“Éclair-san and Liberacion, huh…”
“I wonder if Éclair’s parent learned French somewhere, indeed.”
Looking at the pattern in the naming, it seemed consistent enough that this had to be the case. Judging from Alligator Guy’s explanation, it was likely Éclair’s parent who’d done the naming.
“Well, apparently plenty of modern-day people end up in this world, so I figured that was probably the case with Éclair-san. But is Shion’s name connected to that too?”
“Indeed. Liberacion means liberation, release, freedom—the same meaning as ‘Liberation.’”
It was an odd sort of name, overlapping as it did with the “Liberation” spells belonging to the Hero’s magic.
“A child meant to signify liberation from bloodline, huh… I wonder if it was really a good thing that he met me.”

Alligator Guy himself had spoken of fate earlier too. Father had a distant look in his eyes, as if thinking that had they never met, Alligator Guy might not have had to inherit the curse carried by his lineage as a retainer of the Shield Hero.
“Shield Hero-sama, Liberacion-sama himself takes pride in being a retainer of a Hero. To trouble yourself with such worries would be an insult to him.”
“Waoon.”
“…Yeah. Got it. All right, that’s enough brooding for tonight—let’s get a good night’s sleep.”
And so, for the sake of the Filo-tan Plan set to begin the next day, we all turned in for the night.
The next day, indeed.
“Now then, Father. Make sure you get the scent thoroughly, I say. Big Sister and the rest of the scent-sensitive crowd need to give Father a good, thorough sniff too, indeed.”
“Oh myyy.”

From the morning onward, we moved briskly about our business. First, we’d arranged for Older Sister to accompany Father this time and stay behind in Lute Village. Damage had been kept to a minimum, but apparently she’d help with some of the reconstruction work too. Normally Older Sister looked after Big Sister and the others in Zeltoble or Panda’s village, but this time the arrangement was for her to stay glued to Father’s side for a while.
“Keel, time for the pre-departure scent check on Father, indeed. Make sure no trace of Filolial-sama scent gets on him.”
“Got it, but why’s it bad if some scent gets on him?”
“To avoid the worst-case scenario, apparently, indeed.”

Yes—this was advice from Father in the previous loop. Apparently, if Sakura-chan, the one meant to become Filo-tan, picked up the scent of other Filolial-samas from Father, it could result in a Filo-tan quite different from what he was hoping for.
“And Father, you understand, don’t you?”

“I get it, I get it. Don’t go near the egg once it hatches, even after it’s been entrusted to the Filolials. After it hatches, keep in mind acting standoffish and grumpy. And stay on friendly terms with Sadeena-san.”
“Naofumi-chan, how friendly are you gonna get with Older Sister~?”
Older Sister clung to Father, her voice all sweet and coaxing.
“I feel like that shouldn’t turn into anything that isn’t a joke, if you catch my drift?”
“Oh my? Older Sister thinks it’d be just fine to have some fun with you, Naofumi-chan~.”
“That part’s no problem, I say.”
After all, in the loop where we reunited with Filo-tan on our way back to the first world, there was every possibility that Father and Older Sister had ended up with some kind of relationship.
“No, wait, is that really fine either?”
“Oh myyy.”

Older Sister just laughed, giggling away. At times like this, Older Sister tended to brush everything off as a joke no matter what, so she couldn’t entirely be trusted. Now that I thought about it… when Older Sister carried Father off after we’d reunited with Filo-tan, her hands had been trembling. With Big Sister’s whereabouts unknown and Father being the most important person to her, perhaps Older Sister had sought out that connection out of need. Father from the previous loop had also once murmured, offhandedly, that Older Sister was the lonely type.
